transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um, well, I guess my boss actually suggested I come in. It's... well, I don't want it to sound worse than it is, because I really do try my best at my job. I do general maintenance and repair. But, um, lately I've just had a few little slip-ups. I've been forgetting some scheduled callbacks and, you know, a few work orders. Just basic follow-ups I promised people I'd take care of. 

I feel absolutely awful about letting anyone down, but it just kind of piled up on me recently. Work basically sent me here to, um, get things sorted out before I lose my shot at moving up. I really want to do a good job and get that promotion, so I just want to make sure I'm doing whatever I need to do to fix this. Is that okay? I mean, does that make sense for why I'm here?
Have you struggled with being forgetful or disorganized like this your whole life, or is this a recent change for you?

Um, well... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it's not exactly a new thing. I really don't want it to sound like I'm just making excuses for my work now, but... I do remember being a bit like this way back in grade school, long before I had all this current job pressure. 

My teachers, they were always really sweet and told my parents I was a bright girl, which was nice of them to say! But they also said I was always misplacing my papers, or, you know, missing little parts of the directions when they talked to the class. They usually had to give me extra reminders just to get my classwork finished. 

I promise I was always trying to be a good student and do what I was told, it just... took a little extra effort for me to keep it all straight, I guess. Is it okay that I'm sharing that? I really hope it doesn't make me sound like I've just been irresponsible my whole life.

Looking back at your time in school or even now, did you often find it difficult to stay seated when you were expected to, or did you frequently feel like you were driven by a motor and couldn't sit still?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I was never the type to cause trouble or run around the classroom when I wasn't supposed to. I really always tried to be respectful of the teachers and follow the rules about staying in my seat. 

Even now, I don't really feel... restless like that, or like I have a motor running. I'm usually pretty okay just staying put if that's what I need to do. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
When you are trying to complete a task, do you often find that you are easily distracted by things going on around you, like background noises or other people's conversations?

Um, well... I guess I wouldn't say I'm easily distracted by those kinds of things. I really try to stay focused on whatever I'm doing, especially at work because I don't want to mess up. 

If there's a lot going on, like people talking or machines running, I might notice it, but I don't think it pulls me away from my work any more than it would anyone else. I mean, I really try to tune it out and just keep my head down. I hope that makes sense? I'm not trying to say I have perfect concentration, but I don't think background noise is a big problem for me. Is that what you were asking?
When you have a complex project or a series of tasks to complete, do you often find it difficult to organize your materials or plan out the steps required to finish them?

Um, well... I guess I wouldn't say I have a really hard time organizing things. I mean, in my line of work—doing maintenance and repairs—you sort of have to have a system, right? So I really try my best to keep my tools together and know what order to fix things in. 

I really don't want it to sound like I'm completely scattered or anything. Sometimes, if there's a really big job with a lot of moving parts, I might have to stop and think about it for a minute, but I always get it done. I always try to make sure everything is put away where it belongs when I'm finished, too. I hope that's the kind of thing you're asking about? I really do try to stay on top of my projects.
In your daily life or at work, do you often find that you lose or misplace items that you need to get your job done, such as your tools, your keys, or important paperwork?

Um, well... I try really hard to keep track of everything. I know how important it is to be responsible with my equipment. But, um... I guess lately, I have been having a little trouble with that. 

I mean, I don't want you to think I'm completely disorganized, but... I do find myself hunting for things a lot. Like my tablet for work orders, or my keys, or my flashlight. Sometimes it's even just the tool I was holding like, a minute ago. I'll set it down and then I just... can't find it. 

It's been happening a bit more than I'd like to admit, and it's starting to hold up my jobs sometimes. I really hate it because it makes me look careless, and I'm honestly trying my best to keep it all together. I hope you don't think I'm just being irresponsible? I really do try to keep track of my things.
Aside from the trouble with misplacing items, do you find that you often make careless mistakes in your work tasks because you might have overlooked small details?

Oh, um... no, I really don't think I do that. I mean, I try really, really hard to be thorough. In maintenance, if you overlook a detail, it can cause a bigger problem later, and I definitely don't want my boss or the tenants thinking I do shoddy work. 

So I always try to take my time and double-check things as I go. I might have to look over a work order a couple of times just to be absolutely sure I didn't miss a step, but I wouldn't say I make careless mistakes. I really pride myself on doing a good job and being reliable with the actual repairs. I hope that makes sense? I just always want to make sure I'm doing things the right way so nobody is disappointed in me.
In your day-to-day life, outside of your work responsibilities, do you find that you frequently forget to do routine things, like returning phone calls, paying bills on time, or keeping appointments?

Um... well, I really try to be responsible with my personal stuff, like paying my bills and everything. I never want to be a hassle to anyone. But... um... since you brought up returning phone calls and keeping appointments... I guess I should just be honest. 

That's actually sort of what brought me in to see you today. I hate to admit it because I really, really want my bosses to think well of me, but... I keep forgetting scheduled callbacks. And some work orders, and just... basic follow-ups I promised people. I always have the best intentions, I really do! But it’s just piled up so much lately. 

Actually, my work is the one who sent me here. There's a chance for me to move up, and they want me to get this under control before I lose my shot at the promotion. I really hope you don't think I'm just slacking off or ignoring people on purpose? I promise I'm trying so hard to fix it so I don't let anyone down.
When you are working on a task or project, do you often find that your attention shifts or drifts away before you have actually finished the work?

Um, well... I'd say I'm usually pretty good at sticking with things. I mean, I know how important it is to finish what I start, especially when someone is waiting on a repair. I really don't want to leave a job half-done and make a mess for the tenants. 

So, um, no, I don't think I really drift off like that. I try to just put my head down and get the work done. Sometimes I might have to pause to go grab a different tool or check on something else, but I always make sure the job itself gets finished. I really want to be seen as someone who follows through, you know? I hope that answers your question okay? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right information.
